dataset.name: LongMemEval_S (cleaned)
dataset.setting: S: each question comes with its whole chat history, about 50 sessions and 115k tokens, most of it unrelated

sample.selection: 25 questions of each of the six types, chosen by a hash of the question id before any system was run

reader.prompt: the official LongMemEval chain-of-thought reading prompt, with the question date

judge.prompt: the official LongMemEval per-type judge prompts

hive.label: HivemindOS shared brain
hive.configuration: The prompt-hook recall as shipped: dated past-conversation exchanges ordered by TypeSafe's Jev decision model (Turbo mode, on by default for cloud turns), then the other recalled notes, 5,000 characters at most.

sibyl.label: Sibyl-Memory
sibyl.configuration: The MCP memory_search default (multi_record_search, 10 results, 1,500 characters each), reconstructed in JavaScript from the MIT-licensed source at Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory 761bfc6, with conversation turns stored the way its Hermes adapter journals them.

references.evidenceOnlyNote: The same reader handed only the sessions that contain the answer, with no memory system: the Oracle setting behind Sibyl-Memory's published 95.6%.

limitations: One reader model; absolute scores move with the reader, the comparison between systems is the result.
150 questions: about plus or minus 4 points on one system; the paired counts are the test of the difference.
The Sibyl-Memory arm is a reconstruction of its search from source, not its package; a different way of storing conversations in it could score differently.
LongMemEval measures memory of past conversations; typed memories and vault notes are measured separately on this page.
